Original Prey game you were a native American living in the middle of no where on some shitty reservation. Aliens abduct your girlfriend so you willingly get abducted to go and try and save her. The game is filled with physics puzzles, gravity puzzles, etc. You had some sort of spirit ability where your spirit would go to another world and learn new techniques, and you could then use the spirit ability in real world to solve puzzles.

The new Prey looks like a generic "we're in the science lab with aliens and they're escaping! OH NO!!" storyline. It's a generic CURRENTYEAR+20 atmosphere with a generic storyline where you appear to be the big hero that stops the alien's invasion. A big slap in the face from originally being a game where you're just some random Native American who is struggling to save his girlfriend who has been abducted by aliens.

I understand why people are mad. This is typical Bethesda bullshit where they buy a game studio with a good franchise, gut what made it great, and then rename it the same exact thing to try and make it look like the original never existed. It's exactly what they did with nuDoom. People who aren't familiar with the older version of the game don't care that much, but the long time fans get mad as hell.

I'm annoyed at Bethesda the most about this. They used to just buy existing game franchises and dumb them down for mass consumption. But they'd at least keep it clear it was a sequel. Their new plan is to just rename it the same as the old games and to pretend the old games don't exist, while cherry picking the good ideas from the previous games.

It's a huge disgrace to the original developer's work and vision and they can fuck off forever for doing it. And no, I don't think I'm acting entitled. I'm angry Bethesda keeps raping old franchises and claiming them as their own by pretending they're not even a sequel. Original Prey was a really good game, and this is an embarrassment.

However I am quite pleased with how 1.0 has turned out. I spent a lot of time in terraria and while it has tons of combat and pretty good construction, starbound is different enough and the construction is a lot less tedious than in terraria. Exploring around in starbound is actually pretty rewarding.

That's just how it is with early access. With regular games, it isn't even announced until about a year of pre-alpha development has already happened. Starbound's early access was actually managed quite well in hindsight. They did take the feedback of people who bought early access into account during development, but they also wisely knew when to stick to their own vision, instead of letting the screaming of a divided, unpleasable fanbase dictate everything.

I don't know whether the whole game is scripted or whether the same "missions" happen at the same time because I have the tutorial on.
